title: DataHub: a self-hosted, schema-driven catalogue for simulation and experimental data with knowledge graph and parameter-sweep design
description: DataHub is a self-hosted, containerised catalogue for numerical simulation results and experimental data. Each instance is configured for its project by a YAML project schema that declares dataset types, typed parameters and their sources, file classes, quantities of interest, field embeddings and graph rules, so no code changes are needed. It combines an S3-compatible object store, PostgreSQL with pgvector, a Neo4j knowledge graph, a FastAPI web dashboard, a machine-learning service, a Python client and a command-line tool. Features include full-text, parameter and quantity search; field readers for VTK, NumPy, HDF5, XDMF and Exodus II; similarity graphs from parameter vectors and incremental-PCA field embeddings; parameter-sweep coverage analysis with Sobol, Latin hypercube, random and Gaussian-process suggestions; access control per dataset through roles, organisations and project groups; time-limited sharing links; and download audit logs. The release was hardened after a documented security assessment. The design, methods, security model and evaluation are described in the accompanying technical note (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23378345).
